name: Architecture (two-tier vs direct)
notes: BIS recommends two-tier and advises against direct; most central bank laws do not allow current accounts for the public, so most designs are two-tier.

name: Account-based vs token-based
notes: BIS 2021 favours account-based on digital ID; NY Fed economists say the categories overlap; IMF reframes as proprietary title and nature of platform accounts; RBI preferred token-based for retail.

name: Ledger technology
notes: RBI did not consider DLT suitable at present for throughput reasons; a unified ledger may or may not use DLT.

name: Offline payments
notes: Mitigations: holding limits, forward-transaction limits, time-offline limits, secure hardware; law must define offline finality (draft digital euro: final when local storage updated); e₹ offline not yet available.

name: Privacy and data access
options: managed anonymity (small value anonymous, high value traceable)
notes: Must be compatible with AML/CFT; PETs add latency and complexity; separate payment services from control over data.

name: Holding and transaction limits
notes: Caps must be grounded in law; examples: earlier BoE GBP 10,000 to 20,000; China tiered by ID; eNaira NGN 120,000 to 5,000,000.

name: Remuneration and fees
notes: Most projects unremunerated; e-CNY bank-wallet balances earn deposit interest from 1 Jan 2026; draft digital euro provides free basic services.

name: Programmability
options: programmable money (use restrictions encoded in currency)
notes: IMF: programmable money largely rejected; BoE commits to prohibit programmable money; India allows sponsor-set expiry, geo, MCC and merchant VPA restrictions.

name: Interoperability (domestic and point of sale)
notes: A BoE PoC indicated existing EMV terminals could in principle initiate CBDC payments without modification; e₹ via UPI-QR settles on UPI timelines.

name: Cross-border (multi-CBDC)
notes: mBridge (single system), Icebreaker (hub-and-spoke), Dunbar (multi-CBDC prototypes), Agorá (unified ledger with tokenised reserves and deposits).

name: Legal considerations
notes: IMF: central bank must have statutory authority; Jamaica and India amended laws; Nigeria mandates distribution; EU draft gives ECB portability power.
